A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VPPO research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, proofs, and appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original VPPO training and evaluation results at 7B and 32B scales, component ablations, training dynamics, and qualitative analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds baseline comparisons, design ablations, out-of-domain VQA evaluation, and computational-efficiency experiments.

M1.justification: The proposed VPPO procedure retains KL-based visual dependency, trajectory advantage shaping, binary token filtering, and the same objective and algorithm steps. Soft-mask and reward-shaping alternatives are evaluated as ablations rather than adopted into the main method.

E1.justification: ViRL39K training and the eight original reasoning benchmarks remain. Section 5.3 and Table 8 add A-OKVQA-val and SimpleVQA-EN, substantially extending evaluation to unseen, out-of-domain knowledge and factual VQA tasks.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds GRPO and DAPO to the 32B comparison, which previously included the base model, MM-Eureka, and NoisyRollout. Tables 6–7 also introduce soft-mask and reward-shaping comparators, expanding direct tests of VPPO's advantages and design choices.

E3.justification: The retained reasoning experiments keep the original training and exact-match avg@8 settings. New controls include extending 7B DAPO training from 15.5 to 17 hours to match VPPO's time budget, and calibrating the soft mask to mean weight 0.4 to control update magnitude.

E4.justification: v2 adds tests of VPPO on GRPO, binary versus soft filtering, advantage versus reward shaping, out-of-domain transfer, and equal-time efficiency. These substantially strengthen mechanism and generalization analyses. The original entropy, perturbation, dependency-metric, rollout-size, and qualitative studies remain.

E5.justification: The avg@8 reporting practice is retained. Neither version reports training-seed replication, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests; the new experiments do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: The original VPPO averages remain 57.5 at 7B and 64.6 at 32B. New results include 32B GRPO/DAPO averages of 62.6/63.5, GRPO-based VPPO at 54.8, soft-mask and reward-shaping variants at 56.2/56.8, and VQA results. Appendix J adds runtime, throughput, and equal-budget results.

T1.justification: Appendix I newly defines the calibrated soft mask mathematically, including standardized scores and a sigmoid-offset constraint enforcing mean weight 0.4. The central dependency definition, Theorem 3.1, four assumptions, and variance-reduction proof remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same token-perception findings, hierarchical VPPO contribution, performance claims, and 7B/32B scalability claims. Additional experiments support these claims without redefining the main contribution.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations linking binary filtering to stronger noise rejection, advantage shaping to greater stability, VQA transfer to visual grounding, and equal-budget performance to learning efficiency. These refine the existing interpretation; the substantive limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendices I–J add soft-mask implementation details and runtime/throughput information. Hardware reporting changes from eight H800 GPUs for 7B and 32 for 32B to Appendix B's claim that all models used eight; Table 14 still specifies 32 for 32B, leaving an internal inconsistency. Core hyperparameters and the repository address remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations for the VQA benchmarks and several video-grounding/localization works, while removing works including Intern-S1, FrameThinker, and OpenThinkImg. The central positioning against data-centric, reward-centric, and entropy-based approaches remains.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and section organization are retained. Changes include expanded entropy-selection explanations, consistent dependency terminology in Algorithm 1, ethics/reproducibility/LLM-use statements, and updated author and conference-header text.

P2.justification: Six new tables present the added ablations, VQA results, computational overhead, and equal-budget comparison. Table 1 gains comparison rows, and several main tables are reformatted. Existing figures and qualitative displays retain their content, with some relocated.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses important validation gaps through direct 32B GRPO/DAPO comparisons, controlled design ablations, and an equal-17-hour experiment showing VPPO at 57.5 versus DAPO at 55.0. Together with out-of-domain VQA testing, these materially strengthen attribution, efficiency, and generalization evidence. The conflicting 32B hardware disclosures weaken reproducibility, and uncertainty reporting remains absent, but these limitations do not outweigh the stronger empirical validation.
